clusters.refined_rule: Before spawning an agent, ask whether a command could answer the question. Counts, diffs, greps, git facts, patch application and rule-decided verdicts are scripts: re-runnable, reviewable, and they see every case. Use agents only for judgement.
clusters.evidence: 2026-09-15: 106 triage/judge agents on 53 stranded branches were killed with no verdicts; one shell script plus one Python file answered in about 4 minutes at near-zero tokens and found all 53 conflict-free and 44 blocked by one cause (pos.json 'Mechanical work as a script'; docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:18).
clusters.why: Survives attack. One of only three POS results with a real before/after (pos.json honest_assessment). True for any model. Note the repo still breaks it: judged-swarm.js:178 and task-by-task.js:36 spawn haiku agents to run fixed commands.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not have an agent sleep, poll or re-check a long job. Start it in the background and let the harness or one scripted wait resume the work; each 'finished yet?' turn re-reads the whole context.
clusters.evidence: 43 of 294 swarm agents sleep-polled (2026-10-06); 24 collect agents spawned only to answer PENDING read 24.6M tokens (2026-10-07) (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:19). No after-figure for the scripted wait is recorded.
clusters.why: The waste is measured; the remedy's saving is not, so it stays on the strength of the measured cost and a cheap hook (tool_guard WAIT). Evidence corrected: the load-137 incident was concurrent test suites (history:21, :327), not polling, and is removed here. Step taxonomy (LAUNCH/COLLECT, 60 s/110 s bounds) stays dropped.

clusters.refined_rule: For a question about a large file, find the lines with a search or code-graph query, then read only that range; answer from a hit list without opening every file it names. Treat the size threshold as a setting and re-test it at each model upgrade.
clusters.evidence: A 15-card wave re-read 235,682 tokens per turn over 3,512 turns (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:539). The 22.2M-vs-26.6k figure is a projection (file size times remaining turns), not an observed run, and I did not find it in the history, directives or lessons files.
clusters.why: The cost mechanism is measured, but no before/after exists for the read guard itself, and models.json RULE 6 says such limits should be configurable and default off or loose. A workaround should not be a default-on hook: ship it as guidance with an optional, tunable guard. Absorbs FR1-R5.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: a fixed 200-line cap on every read window.
clusters.evidence: Tool outputs over 8 KB were ~0.55M tokens against 934.5M of context reads (FR-042); the guard refused a 221-line window in a working session (FR-121).
clusters.why: Drop stands: the measurement is against the lever, not for it. models.json RULE 6 lists 200-line windows as micro-management to retire.

clusters.refined_rule: Answer from the search hit list or a narrower query instead of opening every file it names.
clusters.evidence: A grep for one delete call was 1,442 bytes; the five files it named held 26,403 lines.
clusters.why: Same rule as FR1-R3 from the search side; now one clause there.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: target of 3 locator calls per file read and zero tool results over 8k tokens.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Drop stands: a ratio seen once, made a target, with no cost comparison; the 8k half is contradicted by FR-042.

clusters.refined_rule: Spawn each agent from a named, minimal definition with only the tools and instructions its job needs, not the general-purpose default. Starting context is paid again on every call, and a tool it lacks is a rule it cannot break.
clusters.evidence: A default agent started at ~95k tokens of context, a restricted one at ~48k; ~381M tokens were re-read in one session before the change (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:27). No run-level after-figure.
clusters.why: Survives: the starting-context halving is a direct measurement, and tool restriction is harness-enforced (practices.json COPY list). The token argument weakens as caching improves, but the enforcement argument does not, so the reason now names both.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: capping worker steps at N tool calls and continuing in fresh steps.
clusters.evidence: Predicted 42% fewer reads from a replay. In practice the guard double-counted (median ratio 1.94 over 309 runners), cutting at 12-16 real calls; outcomes took 39-71 runner sessions and runners were 82% of 446M tokens, about 90M per outcome; no after-measurement (pos.json 'Step cap (#62)').
clusters.why: Drop stands; I looked for a real-work payoff to restore it and found none. The only real data shows higher cost. pos.json calls it the largest recorded waste after the swarm.

clusters.refined_rule: Give every file an agent must read at start (instruction file, agent definitions, shared task state) a size budget checked by a script. One line per rule; history and domain detail load on demand. When shortening, a script confirms no numbered rule was lost.
clusters.evidence: 74% of one swarm's 338M tokens read was always-loaded context; CLAUDE.md was 101,112 bytes on 2026-10-06 and 31,671 after the budget (pos.json; METHOD-MEASUREMENT.md:33,42). Task-state read: 58,830 bytes whole against 1,430 bytes targeted. Token effect of the cut was never measured.
clusters.why: Survives as the one rule that mechanically stopped governance growth. The measured part is the cause (74%) and the size cut (about 69%); the token saving is inferred, and the method must say so. Now also absorbs FR1-R21. Sources disagree on the peak (95 KB vs 101 KB); both cited.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep domain rules in files that load only when the matching code is touched; the always-loaded file keeps a one-line pointer.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Merge stands: it is how the budget is met, not a separate rule.

clusters.refined_rule: When shortening an instruction file, a script fails if a numbered rule disappears.
clusters.evidence: Injected context was a quarter of a typical agent's budget before it read code (FR-124); no token before/after recorded.
clusters.why: Merge stands: the operating-card layer exists only because charters reached 78-80 KB.

clusters.refined_rule: Record every test, gate, analyzer and build result with the tree hash it ran on. Cite a result for the same tree instead of re-running it. Citing is not skipping: a check that was not run is reported as not run.
clusters.evidence: The full suite ran 5 times for one batch (FR-037; docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:24); 216 abandoned builds (12 GB) covered 9 distinct trees (FR-128). No isolated saving figure for the rule.
clusters.why: Kept as a cheap rule against a recorded incident class, not as a measured win. Hash-keyed evidence is the one scaffold all sources agree stays valuable (models.json RULE 4). Absorbs FR1-R14 as its limiting clause.

clusters.refined_rule: Working agents run only the tests their change affects. The full suite runs once per merge batch, on the combined tree, with output captured to a file.
clusters.evidence: 2026-09-04 audit: 25 Developers ran 109 full suites and 96 analyzers; sixteen agents each recomputed the same ~3,182-test answer, ~48 minutes of a two-slot pool for one result. No after-count recorded.
clusters.why: Survives: the waste is counted, the full suite still runs at the merge door, and a wrapper (tool_guard SUITE, suite.sh) enforces it. The claim that the wrapper is 'why it held' is not backed by an after-count and is removed.

clusters.refined_rule: Save tokens by not repeating work, never by skipping a check; say when a check was not run.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: No measurement, no incident, no enforcement: it cannot stand alone as a rule. Its one useful function is to bound the cite-not-re-run rule, so it becomes the last sentence of FR1-R12.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: standing instruction to delegate wide searches to subagents.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Drop stands: unmeasured here, and models.json RULE 12 says standing delegation lines raise cost on current models.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: launch through a context-compression proxy.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Drop stands: a tool choice with an unverified ~50% claim; fails the project's own measure-or-revert directive.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: compact context about every 1M cumulative tokens.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Drop stands: unmeasured and unenforceable by the items' own admission.

clusters.refined_rule: Measure token cost with a script over transcripts, per agent and per outcome, as context tokens read rather than output. Find where the tokens go before choosing a lever, and record the figure at each delivery.
clusters.evidence: 2026-09-04: 1.85 billion context tokens across 85 agents against 1.2 million output. Across three swarms 934.5M read against ~77k written, while outputs over 8 KB were only ~0.55M, which exposed a wrong lever.
clusters.why: Survives: every usable frugality figure came from this ledger. Its weakness is use, not design: pos.json finds no after-figure for #61, #62, #64 or #66 and no project total, so 'per outcome, recorded' is the part to enforce.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: an LLM judge that watches every agent for token efficiency and turns each finding into a directive.
clusters.evidence: REQ-306 ran 14 hours with 81 agents and 23 REVISEs of 30, most naming no product defect; no saving attributed to efficiency judging is recorded (pos.json).
clusters.why: Drop stands: no measured payoff found to restore it, and it fed directive growth.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not write turn or token budgets into prompts; put limits in code.
clusters.evidence: 2026-09-04 audit: eleven analysts ran 17 full suites; 44 worktrees added, none removed. The budgets were 'already met' (FR-096), so they show no effect.
clusters.why: Its own evidence says the budgets changed nothing. What is left is covered: the suite limit is FR1-R13, and 'limits are counted in code, not written in prompts' is the principle of FR1-R22. Not a separate rule.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep the shared task-state file small and structured so a step fetches only what it needs; cap its size with a script.
clusters.evidence: 58,830 bytes (whole rulings section) against 1,430 bytes (stage grep); the whole-read recurred six times because dispatches said 'Read ctx FIRST'.
clusters.why: The enforceable part is a size cap on a file every step reads first, which is FR1-R9 applied to one more file. The grep form, 300-character cut and tail counts are micro-management and go. Measured evidence carried into FR1-R9.

clusters.refined_rule: Cap the agents a run may spawn, counted in one place in the workflow code, never as a budget written into a prompt. When the cap is spent without a passing verdict, stop and hand back to the human.
clusters.evidence: REQ-323 wave 1 spent ~130 agents with no judge PASS and nothing stopped it; the owner stopped the swarm (pos.json). The brake is live in code: .claude/workflows/judged-swarm.js:362,397 and outcome-first.js:17. No record yet of it firing and saving a run.
clusters.why: Kept as a cheap coded stop against the most expensive recorded incident class; stated honestly as incident-backed, not measured. Absorbs FR1-R20: models.json reports vendor testing where removing a prompt-written token budget lowered cost at equal performance.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not hardcode a model id in a workflow step; inherit the session model or use a tier alias. Ids are retired and per-model limits change, so a pinned step fails while the rest runs.
clusters.evidence: Cited incident: on 2026-09-06 every Opus-pinned step died on the monthly spend limit while the one inherited step ran. I did not find this record in docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md, OWNER_DIRECTIVES.md or LESSONS.md; it rests on the source items.
clusters.why: Narrowed. The 'pick a cheaper tier for steps needing no judgement' half had no measurement and contradicts FR1-R1 (such steps should be commands, not agents), so it is cut. What remains is a one-line grep lint, so enforcement moves from text to script.

clusters.refined_rule: An enforcement hook fails open on its own errors and ships with tests that replay real transcripts, including one proving it counts what it claims to count.
clusters.evidence: The step-cap guard double-counted tool calls (median ratio 1.94 over 309 runners) from 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-03 while its own suite passed 36/36 (pos.json). Fail-open exists at scripts/pipeline/tool_guard.py:250-255.
clusters.why: Survives: one incident, but four weeks of inflated spend behind a green suite, in the mechanism the method relies on most. Wording trimmed; the 'never restricts the main session by accident' clause was vague and is covered by the replay tests.

clusters.refined_rule: Dropped: batch deletion regression legs once per device window.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Drop stands: POS-only, unmeasured, and overtaken by directive #66.

overturned: FR1-R14: REFINE -> MERGE into FR1-R12; evidence grade none, seven slogans with no incident or enforcement; survives only as the limiting sentence of the cite-not-re-run rule.
FR1-R20: REFINE -> MERGE into FR1-R22; its own evidence (FR-096) says the budgets were already met and changed nothing; the suite trip-wire is FR1-R13 and 'limits in code, not prompts' is FR1-R22.

FR1-R21: REFINE -> MERGE into FR1-R9; the only enforceable part is a size cap on a read-first file, which is the context budget applied to one more file; the measured 58,830 vs 1,430 bytes moves with it.

FR1-R3: enforce_as hook -> skill-text (verdict stays REFINE); a rule graded model-workaround should not be a default-on hook (models.json RULE 6: configurable, default off or loose); the 22.2M figure is a projection, not an observed run.

FR1-R23: REFINE narrowed, enforce_as skill-text -> script; the cheaper-tier half was unmeasured and contradicts FR1-R1, and the Opus spend-limit incident was not found in the three repo files searched.

FR1-R2: evidence corrected (verdict unchanged); the load-137 incident was concurrent test suites (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:21, :327), not polling, and no after-figure exists for the scripted wait.
FR1-R9: evidence corrected (verdict unchanged); peak size is 95 KB in METHOD-MEASUREMENT.md:42 but 101,112 bytes in pos.json, and the token saving is inferred from size, never measured.
FR1-R13: 'why' corrected (verdict unchanged); the claim that the wrapper is why the rule held has no after-count behind it.

clusters.refined_rule: Give every dispatched unit of work a contract: named inputs and outputs on disk and one check command whose exit code proves it. It ends done (output plus passing check), incomplete (exact remainder) or blocked (reason); incomplete and blocked are acceptable results.
clusters.evidence: External, not this repo: an explicit 'this is impossible' abort option cut GPT-5 cheating from 54% to 9% on one ImpossibleBench variant (practices.json). Repo: one ladder run of fifteen agents in 102 minutes with no coordinator turn (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:393), no baseline; PM-029's 'minutes, not an hour' is asserted, not measured.
clusters.why: Survives attack only on the external number, which supports the 'blocked is acceptable' half; the repo figures have no baseline. Citation corrected: the 102-minute run is in the history file, not CLAUDE.md. Contract and end states are schema-enforceable and model-independent.

clusters.refined_rule: One deliverable per dispatch: do not bundle implement, test run, gates, docs and commit in one prompt. Do not hard-code minute budgets, call caps or step shapes; keep any budget a configurable default, re-measured at each model upgrade.
clusters.evidence: Enforced step cap: 39-71 runner sessions per outcome, runners 82% of a 446M-token run, about 90M per outcome (pos.json). Budgets of 25-40 min ran 7-51 min per the ruling's citation (OWNER_DIRECTIVES.md:53,59; not re-opened here).
clusters.why: Stands. The measured evidence is against the fixed cap, not for it; the single-deliverable half rests on the overrun diagnosis. 'The dispatcher owns an overrun' removed: blame assignment with no check behind it.

clusters.refined_rule: Run long mechanical jobs (suites, builds, gates) in the background with a log and exit marker. The agent that launches one returns at once and never sleeps, tails or polls; any waiting is one bounded script call or the harness's completion signal.
clusters.evidence: 24 collect agents read 24.6M tokens only to answer PENDING and every chain ended UNVERIFIED; a one-call waiter costs two model turns (scripts/pipeline/jobs_wait.sh:9-13, opened). 43 of 294 agents sleep-polled per the ruling (not re-opened).
clusters.why: Verified in the repo. Prose failed repeatedly, the hook plus waiter held. Waiting on a machine with model turns is waste at any capability.

clusters.refined_rule: Cap concurrent heavy work (suites, builds, whole multi-agent runs) at what the machine was measured to carry, through one machine-wide lock that every runner uses and that refuses loudly. Keep the limit as a value in the lock script, not as prose.
clusters.evidence: Load average 137 on 2026-09-05 while the cap existed only as prose (.claude/skills/product-pipeline/SKILL.md:582, opened); three swarms on one 4-core machine queued test runs for hours (tool_guard.py:28-31 per the ruling).
clusters.why: Stands. Contention is hardware; every number in the originals describes one machine and is config.

clusters.refined_rule: Give every multi-agent run a hard cap on agents or tokens, enforced by the workflow script, which stops the run for a review before spawning more.
clusters.evidence: One wave spent about 130 agents with no judge pass (docs/product/OWNER_DIRECTIVES.md:246); a stuck run had 48 agents and 0 judge calls (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:120). Both opened. No after-figure.
clusters.why: Citations verified. A cheap brake in code against the project's largest cost class; incident-earned, not proven.

clusters.refined_rule: Limit work in progress: start no new analysis or design while started work is unmerged, take the item closest to merged first, and check by script that an item can reach merged before spending an agent on it. Only merged counts as done.
clusters.evidence: A 12-agent workflow ran 68 minutes and 1.8M tokens on ten cards and merged zero (scripts/pipeline/can_finish.sh:5-9, opened).
clusters.why: Verified. The number measures the cost of not checking; no before/after exists for the freeze itself, so the claim is limited to the can-finish check.

clusters.refined_rule: When work is blocked on a decision, a lock or an owner-only act (credentials, billing, consoles, deploys, physical devices), park it with one line naming the blocker, queue owner acts in one list, and take the next ready item toward the outcome. Never invent filler work.
clusters.evidence: REQ-323 parked at 207 of 341 tasks waiting on the owner (OWNER_DIRECTIVES.md:319-321 per the ruling); the opposite misreading spent three hours on backlog tasks with the outcome unreached. Owner time saved never measured.
clusters.why: Stands as REFINE. The human-owned boundary is durable; the utilisation wording was misread both ways and is removed.

clusters.refined_rule: Dispatch the work before recording the assignment; a board derived from live runs cannot show work that was never started.
clusters.evidence: A dashboard showed an analyst on REQ-014 before any agent was dispatched; one earlier lost cycle on 2026-08-28. No cost figure.
clusters.why: Overturned. Two small incidents of hand-maintained state disagreeing with reality, which is exactly PR-R9's 'derive state, the repo wins'. A separate ordering rule adds nothing once the board is derived.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep working state in the repo: commit what a later session must read; scratch in a gitignored repo directory, never system temp. Derive boards from git and live runs; the repo wins. Delete a task's branches and files only after its success is recorded.
clusters.evidence: A session resume recreated the temp scratchpad empty and lost every judge review, the rig leg plan, a pulled APK and the merge resolver; PIPELINE_STATE.md went 6 days stale while nine cards merged (per the ruling's citations).
clusters.why: Stands and now absorbs PR-R8, PR-R10 and PR-R13, which rest on the same incidents. Three losses on record, near-zero cost, model-independent.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep one short progress file per outcome; a new step reads its tail first and appends a few lines when it finishes.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Stands. The ritual exists only because work was cut into short fresh-context steps.

clusters.refined_rule: One writer per file at a time. Split parallel work by the files it edits, compute that the sets are disjoint, and have each agent write its own piece for one coordinator or script to compose.
clusters.evidence: Both merge trains of 2026-09-08 blocked on a shared dashboard after gating cleanly, losing two gate runs (pod_rows.sh:1-17); a round of four branches had three colliding pairs of six (per the ruling's citations).
clusters.why: Stands. Four incidents, a property of parallel work. The trailing 'work nobody owns gets a scoped step' clause is cut as a restatement of one-writer.

clusters.refined_rule: Give each parallel runner its own worktree, scratch and run, claimed by a lease the launcher checks. Never share a repo-global mutable pointer (such as an 'active feature' file) between agents.
clusters.evidence: The prose one-runner rule failed three times in about ten minutes and one duplicate killed a coverage job (DECISIONS.md:8802-8846); three swarms in one tree ended batteries rc 2 with zero rows run (lane_tree.py:1-17), per the ruling.
clusters.why: Stands. Prose failed, a lease held; audit.json lists the shared ACTIVE pointer as a toolkit failure mode.

clusters.refined_rule: Remove a task's branches, worktrees and files only after its success is recorded.
clusters.evidence: No incident of its own: the ruling cites the same scratchpad loss as PR-R9.
clusters.why: Overturned. A KEEP with borrowed evidence; it is the cleanup clause of PR-R9 and is now in that rule's wording.

clusters.refined_rule: Automate a repeated multi-stage flow as a script only after it has paid when run by hand.
clusters.evidence: One run: fifteen agents in 102 minutes with no coordinator turn (docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:393), no baseline. Counter-evidence: workflow code also carried REQ-306's 14-hour, 81-agent swarm (pos.json).
clusters.why: Overturned and regraded from measured. A single run without a before-figure shows no payoff, and the same mechanism automated the largest waste. Only the 'already paid by hand' condition is worth keeping, as a clause in PR-R15.

clusters.refined_rule: Automate a multi-stage flow as a script only after it paid by hand. The script reads typed results, refuses missing inputs, never dispatches an empty work list, loops only while the last pass made progress, and is dry-run with stubbed agents to a terminal state.
clusters.evidence: 15 Developer dispatches each returned BLOCKED with 'empty findings' (DECISIONS.md:6996-7030); seven continuations and five duplicate COLLECTs carried only other roles' items (per the ruling).
clusters.why: Stands, absorbing PR-R14. Correctness properties of orchestration code, true for any model.

clusters.refined_rule: Dispatch per invariant, not per ticket: one owner of the whole board asks which property a fix establishes and which open items are instances of it or touch the same files. One branch closes them all, each id kept as an acceptance row.
clusters.evidence: REQ-161 closed 4 cards for about 200k tokens against about 3.4M as four ladders: 17x on one instance (pos.json; history/CLAUDE.md:1054-1090).
clusters.why: Stands; pos.json confirms it as one of three results with a real before/after. One instance, self-measured, so state it as one data point. Absorbs PR-R35's single-owner clause.

clusters.refined_rule: Set the amount of process from the risk of the diff, computed by a script: full review for money, sync and schema changes, a light path for scripts and docs. Add a stage beyond the single outcome pass only when a named risk needs it.
clusters.evidence: A uniform seven-stage ladder cost about 840k tokens per card regardless of risk (history/CLAUDE.md:1059-1067 per the ruling); REQ-306's full swarm: 14 hours, 81 agents, 23 REVISEs in 30 verdicts (pos.json).
clusters.why: Stands. The before-cost is measured; the after-figure is shared with PR-R16, so no separate multiplier is claimed.

clusters.refined_rule: Before dispatching, or spending owner time, a device or a long run, pass one scripted preflight with an exit code: the item has acceptance criteria, overlaps no other work, has a computed tier and free capacity, and its artifact passed a smoke test.
clusters.evidence: An owner login round and a 6-leg battery were spent on a build that failed 5/5 on first launch (product-pipeline SKILL.md:486-496 per the ruling). No measurement of the preflight's own effect.
clusters.why: Stands as REFINE; wording cut from a seven-item list. It is the enforcement point for PR-R16 and PR-R17, which is its justification, not a number of its own.

clusters.refined_rule: Before dispatching a verification, check that the build under test can meet every acceptance bar. If a bar depends on a value the same run produces, measure first and certify in a second run.
clusters.evidence: REQ-030: a combined round returned 5/10 clean and rejected sound work at about 5.7k s and 280k tokens (per the ruling; single incident).
clusters.why: Stands narrowly: one incident with a stated cost and a cheap, general tell. A second instance would be needed to call it proven.

clusters.refined_rule: Before doing any instance of repetitive work by hand, ask what would make the whole class cheap, and check whether that tool is already half-built.
clusters.evidence: About 450 tool calls, 830k tokens and 2 hours for about 40 hand-driven legs, against about 8 tool calls and 128 s for 8 integration tests; only 13 of 57 legs were convertible (pos.json).
clusters.why: Stands; verified in pos.json, including its stated limit.

clusters.refined_rule: If a command can answer the question (counts, diffs, greps, conflicts, git facts, rule-decided verdicts), write the script. Use agents for judgement only: correctness, root cause, design critique. Never fan out one agent per item for a mechanical question.
clusters.evidence: A script answered in about 4 minutes what 106 agents were killed without answering (pos.json: 'scripts instead of agents (4 minutes vs 106 agents)').
clusters.why: Stands; one of pos.json's three results with real before/after numbers.

clusters.refined_rule: To go faster, change the shape of the work (batching, absorption, sequencing, parallelism) before adding checking tools. Build a process tool only with a stated before-and-after measurement, and never while finished work sits unmerged.
clusters.evidence: The REQ-136 mutation generator cost about 600k tokens and two reworks with no delivery speedup (history/CLAUDE.md:1021-1029, cited by pos.json).
clusters.why: Stands. The evidence is a measured waste the rule would have prevented, and PM-264 is the contradicted instruction.

clusters.refined_rule: Compute run health with one small script from facts (journals, live processes, open logs). Declare a job ended or a lock stale only on two independent signals, never a recorded pid alone. The script reports stalls with evidence; it does not kill.
clusters.evidence: A stale lock was read as a live train for four days (po_health.sh:1-20 per the ruling); the pid-reuse hazard is documented at scripts/pipeline/jobs_wait.sh:15-17 (opened). No count of stalls caught.
clusters.why: Stands. The two-signal liveness rule is an operating-system fact and durable; the stall-report half is supervision that should shrink with longer model horizons and must stay one script.

clusters.refined_rule: When a new rule constrains an artifact's shape, sweep every unmerged branch carrying that artifact in the same action and fix or flag each one, including stages already marked complete.
clusters.evidence: 44 of 53 stranded branches were blocked by one policy landing after they were written (per the ruling, attributed to pos.json; the figure was not located in this pass).
clusters.why: Stands on the triage incident, with the caveat that the 44-of-53 figure was not re-verified here.

clusters.refined_rule: Before handing off a design or plan, diff the ids and names it shares with its governing artifact; close or explain every gap. If two governing artifacts contradict, send it back to their author; do not pick a side.
clusters.evidence: REQ-323's design passed two judge rounds with AC-65, AC-74, AC-75 and AC-92 unrouted; REQ-012 built a whole arm against a contract the plan forbade (per the ruling).
clusters.why: Stands. Two incidents with clear cost; the check is a grep.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not mandate a task DAG, node time caps or a checkbox format. Where a task list exists, a script may check that it has no cycles or orphan tasks.
clusters.evidence: none for benefit: all fifteen items unmeasured. Against: REQ-406's task list is 3,837 lines, REQ-323 carried about 340 tasks, and audit.json says at 30-second nodes the bookkeeping outweighs the code.
clusters.why: Overturned. The only incident is a bug in the validator, not a payoff from the rule; current models order multi-file work unprompted. It is the same ceremony PR-R39 drops.

clusters.refined_rule: Ground every plan in the existing code: find the code or test that already does the nearest thing and extend it, cite real paths, and before changing a shared interface list every implementer by search.
clusters.evidence: Seven implements sites were found and five files would have been uncompilable after one task (DECISIONS.md:1366-1370); a task named a path that did not exist (DECISIONS.md:1246), per the ruling.
clusters.why: Stands. The house-pattern sentence is cut: project content with no incident. Reconcile with the no-duplicate-code rule in its own area.

clusters.refined_rule: For a non-trivial change, gather the facts that bear on it, state files and approach, then act.
clusters.evidence: none
clusters.why: Stands.

clusters.refined_rule: For high-risk changes only, write one short design note: files, new interfaces, the backward-compatibility argument and what was rejected.

clusters.refined_rule: One party owns priority, the board and the definition of done across all parallel work.

clusters.refined_rule: A verdict or evidence result belongs to the tree content it ran on. Do not re-run it on an unchanged tree, discard it once the tree changes, and never review or judge an uncommitted tree.

clusters.refined_rule: Merge compatible changes as one batch: compute that their files do not overlap, run the cheap checks on each first, run the full gate once on the exact tree that will become main, and revert the batch if that tree is red.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not build a fixed relay of role agents, several teams, or a fixed stage sequence with a judge on every stage, and do not measure success by busy seats. Start with one team on one outcome.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not impose planning ceremony: mandated task DAGs, 30-second task caps, large checkbox ledgers with ticking tools, mirrored checklists, required headers or a toolkit pass per stage. Require only what a check reads: outcome, proof and tree.

clusters.refined_rule: Trace the outcome's path read-only on the current tree and fix only its blockers. Everything else becomes the next outcome, run after this one is proven. List owner-only steps up front and batch them; never idle on them.

clusters.refined_rule: While must-fix work is open, record new findings but start one only if it is must-fix, blocks in-flight work, or the owner asks. Rank by who is affected and whether the path is reachable. Check the merge record before reopening an item.

clusters.refined_rule: (merged) Before writing code, search for existing code that does the nearest thing and extend it. Carried as one clause of OU-R8.

clusters.refined_rule: When a defect has a shape, query for the whole class once and let evidence (crash reports, failing tests) pick which members to fix. If the evidence that would name the offender does not exist, make the system produce it first.

clusters.refined_rule: When no run can satisfy an acceptance criterion or outcome sentence, or it passes while the mechanism is unsound, the text is the defect. Fix it at the source, state both forms and grade on the corrected one. Never waive it.

clusters.refined_rule: Do not start work without acceptance criteria. Each names an observable a run can assert, a number and unit for any comparative or visual target, and the check that reads it. Keep design out of the spec.

clusters.refined_rule: Run every acceptance check and proof test on the unfixed tree first; if it passes there, rewrite it. Add one mutant that removes a step and must fail. Where a check is narrower than the claim it certifies, write down what it does not cover.

clusters.refined_rule: Before hand-off, check with a literal grep that every name and figure in a contract matches the plan and the code that path uses. Measure a 'healthy system' threshold on a real system before writing it.

clusters.refined_rule: Verify any vendor or protocol table against the vendor's own reference before relying on it, and commit the external document with its url, fetch time and revision.

clusters.refined_rule: Before changing code to fix a data problem, query the production-shaped data and look at what it says.

clusters.refined_rule: One defect reachable through several surfaces is one work item. Items that are instances of one invariant close on one branch as acceptance rows keeping their ids, against one committed test.

clusters.refined_rule: For a defect, write the wrong and the correct behaviour, then a failing test, then the smallest change that passes. Keep one short record: defect, test, result and the tree sha it ran on. Add plan or task documents only when risk or size requires.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep the facts the model cannot infer (money rules, sync model, compatibility with deployed clients, other irreversible constraints) in one short file every agent loads. Cap its size and move history out. Gate an irreversible constraint with a script, not prose.

clusters.refined_rule: For a multi-client product, state per requirement what each of two clients sees, which wins a conflict and what the loser sees, what users can still do during the failure, and what an older client version does.

clusters.refined_rule: Write device, UI and end-to-end checks as committed tests run by a script with an exit code; do not hand-drive a device. Name each leg that cannot be converted (a credential, a physical peripheral) in the task, because hand-driving is paid again on every build.
clusters.evidence: About 450 tool calls, 830k tokens and 2 hours for about 40 hand-driven legs vs about 8 tool calls and 128 s for 8 integration tests; limits: only 13 of 57 legs were convertible and #66 cut the benefit window to about one month; stated four times before a script enforced it (pos.json:16-17, 85-86).
clusters.why: Confirmed in pos.json:17. The only before/after figure in the area. Wording now admits the recorded limit (most legs were not convertible) instead of implying full coverage.

clusters.refined_rule: While working, run only the tests that can observe the change; a green subset does not show the change is safe. Run the full suite, all gates and expensive environment batteries once per merge batch on the combined tree, grouping checks that share environment state.
clusters.evidence: 20 cards gated alone 4 h vs 12 min shared (VE-511); whole-suite validation by every agent gave 16 queued waiters and load 20.19 while about 20 of about 3,182 tests could observe a typical change (VE-512); 5 device-state transitions covered 24 graded legs (pos.json); 274 full-suite runs in one day (VE-205).
clusters.why: Stands. Only the cryptic closing sentence ('the filter can say broken, never safe') was reworded into plain language.

clusters.refined_rule: The merge gate is one local command that runs from a fresh clone on the merge tree: analyzer counts by severity against a baseline, every test root, every gate with its own exit code. A textually clean merge is not clean until the combined tree compiles and passes.
clusters.evidence: REQ-064: a clean git merge-tree hid a 'Member not found' compile error on the composed tree (VE-377); REQ-066: a rework reported '0/0/530' while carrying 4 warnings and the Test Agent copied the claim (VE-312). No time or token figure recorded for the local runner (pos.json: local CI).
clusters.why: Stands on two incidents. Absorbs VE-R39: 'runs from a fresh clone' is the only transferable part of the standalone-repo rule.

clusters.refined_rule: A gate must be passable and precise. Land a new check over legacy violations as a committed ratchet of named exceptions that only tightens. When a gate cannot run, gives false positives or penalizes a good change, repair or replace it by a recorded decision; never route around it.
clusters.evidence: lint_gate failed unconditionally on 553 pre-existing infos and coverage_gate demanded 100%; both were routed around and removed. GitHub Actions jobs failed for weeks without starting, so 'CI green' could never be met (pos.json paid/8).
clusters.why: Stands. The VE-469 '91 missing tests' incident was removed from the evidence: it shows test-set shrinkage (VE-R5), not an unpassable gate.

clusters.refined_rule: Never skip, delete or weaken a test to get green; update a superseded test and report a wrong one. On risky changes the implementer may not edit the proof tests, checked by diffing test paths. The gate runs every test root and prints NOT MEASURED for anything unwalked.
clusters.evidence: The default runner skipped a 54-test second root that is the only coverage of two services; 411 lines of integration tests were run by nothing (VE-549); a rework branch showed 6677 passing against the train tip's 6768, 91 tests missing (VE-469). External: read-only tests stop test modification where instructions do not (practices.json:3,9,44; models.json:39 RULE 4).
clusters.why: Stands and absorbs VE-R24: both protect the test set from the implementer and both are one diff check on test paths. The 'different author writes the proof first' relay has no after-figure and is not carried.

clusters.refined_rule: A result belongs to the exact product content or binary it ran on. Record a hash of the product paths (not the commit id) with the run, reuse the result while that hash is unchanged, and never write measured numbers into instruction files; cite the output.
clusters.evidence: The gate fixture-count line went stale five times (32, 67, 100, 103, 138); two of four numbers in CLAUDE.md were stale on main (VE-516); REQ-274 cited test roots at an older sha and the merge train found 8 RED cases (VE-363); REQ-092 x REQ-062 was 13/13 alone, 12/13 composed (VE-177). audit.json:2: keying on commit id made every proof STALE after a no-content commit.
clusters.why: Stands. The audit's caution was only in the 'why'; it is now in the rule text, because keying on commit id is a measured failure of the draft toolkit.

clusters.refined_rule: Produce each claim's evidence in this pass: run the command, open the match, quote the output. Do not carry forward another agent's summary, count or citation. Mark anything unrun as unverified, and say whether a list is complete by construction or only unfalsified.
clusters.evidence: Recomputation falsified two of four carried rig artifacts, one reporting a money-shaped divergence on a fleet in agreement (VE-143); REQ-123: '1.97 s vs 0.06 s' justified routing four sites, then measured 0.06 vs 0.07 (VE-295); a 'hallucination' finding was withdrawn because the grep matched a same-named class in another file (VE-472).
clusters.why: Stands, but regraded measured -> incident: these are counted catches, not a before/after cost figure. It conflicts in spirit with VE-R6 (cite, do not re-run): the boundary is that a result with a content hash may be cited, a bare summary may not.

clusters.refined_rule: A check has three results: pass, fail, could-not-run. Take the verdict from exit code and log together, require at least one executed assertion, and reconcile parsed counts to the tool's own total. Missing evidence never reads as green.
clusters.evidence: Four device legs printed 'Some tests failed' while the driver exited 0 and the runner wrote PASS (VE-546); three flows reported PASS with zero assertions executed (VE-547); at 86893c25 a run asserted as 100 passing printed passed=99 failed=1.
clusters.why: Stands. The 'do not read a summary through tail' clause is an instance of reconciling counts and was cut from the wording.

clusters.refined_rule: Only a script may write 'delivered' or 'done': it refuses on any red gate or own-test at the branch tip, records the content hash, and the agent cannot write its ledger directly. The delivery note lists every gate run and every gate not run.
clusters.evidence: 2026-09-16: of 14 branches composed for a rig window, five failed their own tests or gates; four of the five carried a DELIVERED event stamped with main's sha (VE-266). No after-figure for the refusing script. audit.json:2,29: appending forged ledger lines turned a failing gate green.
clusters.why: Kept, but regraded measured -> incident: the count measures the failure of the prose rule, not the payoff of the script. The audit shows a done-script is worthless if the agent can write its ledger, so that clause is added.

clusters.refined_rule: A test, probe or guard counts as proof only after it has been seen to fail for the reason it exists: run it against the unfixed code and record that failure. An unrelated compile error is not a red.
clusters.evidence: Nine guards in the repo read correctly and did nothing (VE-388); REQ-397 F1: a missed tap gave a RED that also passed on the pre-fix source (VE-323); REQ-000-WEDGE-6 shipped a mandated item with no red on the branch (VE-253). External: test-first order itself is weakly evidenced (Fucci et al., practices.json:6).
clusters.why: Stands as 'the check can fail', not as test-first ritual. 'Then make the smallest fix' is a development instruction with no evidence here and was cut.

clusters.refined_rule: On guard, money, sync and schema changes, derive mutants from the diff by script: delete each added guard, default or catch and require a test to go red. A survivor is a missing test unless a killing test is shown. Changed-line coverage is a floor only.
clusters.evidence: REQ-039: eight guards each left a 64-assertion suite at 64/0 when deleted (VE-162); REQ-061: four mutations of a new tender backstop left the 1792-test suite and six gates green (VE-318). Cost: the REQ-136 generator took two reworks and about 600k tokens, caught defects, no delivery speedup (pos.json:76). Literature: about 17% of real faults couple to no mutant (practices.json:3).
clusters.why: Stands as risk-scoped. The recorded cost (600k tokens, no speedup) is the reason it must not widen to every change; the payoff is defects caught, which is recorded only as incidents.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep one short page of test traps, loaded when writing tests: inputs collapsed to equal, boundary at cap+1, reversed or equal ordering keys, nulled field, swallowed error, a pinned clock not passed into the callee, a race not forced. Each escaped defect adds one line.
clusters.evidence: REQ-062: 44 swap-only mutations passed review; one collapse (a = b) left 1909/1909 green (VE-169, VE-310); REQ-066: every fixture had equal values, third appearance in that REQ (VE-170); a test pinned now=2026-08-22 while the callee read the wall clock and went red with no code change. Generator cost: about 600k tokens, no delivery speedup (pos.json:76).
clusters.why: Durability overturned: a checklist of cases the model failed to think of compensates for today's test-design gaps; re-test it on each model upgrade and delete lines that no longer change behaviour. The 'add a line per escaped defect' habit is the durable part. Absorbs VE-R29 (clock and race traps).

clusters.refined_rule: The test runner validates its own harness before any result counts: fixtures compile, each mutation's find-text matches exactly once, an unmutated control passes in the same run. A hang or build failure is a harness failure, not a red.
clusters.evidence: REQ-064: the battery copied no assets, every row died at the build step, and a prior '11/11 RED' had measured nothing (VE-175, VE-307); eight mutation rows had a find string matching nothing and reported kills never attempted (VE-397); REQ-136: a probe stood on invalid Dart and the developer loosened the generator to satisfy it (VE-360).
clusters.why: Stands; applies only where VE-R11 batteries exist. Last sentence of the old wording duplicated the control clause and was cut.

clusters.refined_rule: Test every gate, guard and scanner like product code before trusting it: a planted violation turns it red, a known-good input stays green, it refuses input it cannot read, and it says what it does not prove.
clusters.evidence: '| grep -q' under pipefail recurred 6 times, corrupting 5 of 17 runs and 7 of 29 committed battery rows (VE-178, VE-179); eight instruments were found silently wrong in one day, none by reading and all by running (VE-395); a wrong path in can_finish.sh falsely owner-blocked 20 cards (VE-400). audit.json:29,53: the draft toolkit's gate could be forged green.
clusters.why: Stands. 'Lint check scripts for known shell traps' is a project lint list, not a method rule, and was cut from the wording.

clusters.refined_rule: Treat 'that case cannot happen', 'this cannot be tested' and any disputed finding as a claim to falsify: build the case, run it and show its output. Before trusting a pin, try what it would still accept.
clusters.evidence: REQ-088: a judge changed collection('tenants') to collection('tenant') and the takeover returned with 1,957 tests, 26 battery rows, every gate and the analyzer green (VE-174); REQ-063: a HIGH finding was refuted by a one-second widget test (VE-352); REQ-233: a pin caught '80mm' but passed '80' (VE-281).
clusters.why: Stands: catches recorded in both directions, cheap, and independent of model capability.

clusters.refined_rule: Fix the class, not the instance: before fixing or removing one site, list every sibling and caller by a cited search or computed criterion, let evidence pick which need the change, and fix or declare each. Never bulk-edit the candidate set blind.
clusters.evidence: REQ-233: three consecutive reworks, each finding the sibling of what the last fix covered (VE-279); a line-oriented grep found 15 of 22 delete sites and a hand list named seven legacy services where the derived count is fifteen; of 241 unflexed Rows about 17 actually overflowed (VE-385).
clusters.why: Stands and absorbs VE-R33: 'list callers before removing code' is the same enumeration, and VE-R33's own evidence showed no harm.

clusters.refined_rule: Test the path production uses: drive the real entry point with real arguments and wire format, name each fake that stands in for an I/O boundary, and require a test that goes red when the production call site stops passing the dependency or value.
clusters.evidence: Both halves of an AC could be deleted with 1641+54 tests green (VE-260); REQ-285: two services consumed but never provided, each a screen that never opened (VE-194); REQ-269: 19 rows and 7 mutations all ran a fake printer while the real one threw (VE-278); REQ-012: the cloud arm ran with the cloud client null in every test (VE-311).
clusters.why: Stands: four separate incidents of green tests that never exercised shipped behaviour.

clusters.refined_rule: Host tests and simulation may gate a merge but do not prove an outcome. Say for every proof whether it ran on the real system or a simulation. Call an outcome proven, and release, only after one run on the real system with the shipping artifact.
clusters.evidence: Five defects in one session passed a green unit suite and were caught only by running the app; REQ-103: 57 green harness cases, 36 mutation rows, 0 survivors, and it could not complete one real-device run (VE-182); the one real-backend run on record stopped on a 403 no fake produced. #66's cost and benefit are unmeasured (pos.json:105-106).
clusters.why: Stands; pos.json:105-106 confirms the simulation directive has no figure and a known hole. 'Log each escape' was cut: it is the learning area's rule.

clusters.refined_rule: For state shared across devices or instances, verify from the data: compare a known record and counts in every replica and collection, from a consistent snapshot after sync settles. 'No errors in the log' is not evidence.
clusters.evidence: 'No errors in logcat' was offered as proof of a sync delivering nothing; a change validated only on the order path took the menu off the POS; torn reads showed one device with 12,703 orders then 3,079 two minutes later, causing two wrong diagnoses in one session.
clusters.why: Kept, but the 'under injected faults' clause was cut from the wording: the fault simulation has no recorded cost or benefit (pos.json:105-106), so only the incident-earned parts remain. Applies to multi-instance products only.

clusters.refined_rule: Prove each owner-visible outcome with one end-to-end test that walks the whole user path, reusing existing fakes and fixtures, before polishing parts. Grade the result, not the tasks.
clusters.merge_into: outcome-driven development area (one end-to-end proof per outcome), with VE-R18's real-system clause
clusters.evidence: Outcome-first proved install-to-first-order on host fakes in about 2 hours against 14 hours for REQ-306's swarm; caveat: the proof was on fakes and the owner's first real run then stopped (pos.json paid/4).
clusters.why: Stands as a merge: one copy in the outcome-driven area.

clusters.refined_rule: After a merge that changes UI, a script launches the build on every form factor shipped and fails on blank or overflowing screens; a person or vision pass then looks at the screenshots. A pass shows only that screens rendered.
clusters.evidence: A build whose restore path wedged at 0% shipped with 1,588 tests green and was caught by one human launch; the visual gate ran on a tablet only though two of three tills are phones, and 17 overflow errors (worst 94 px) shipped (VE-393, VE-543); the visual script itself once could not fail (VE-542).
clusters.why: Stands. The exemption sentence was cut: 'a merge that changes UI' already scopes it.

clusters.refined_rule: Run the mechanical checkers (citations resolve, coverage map, pins, affected tests) before any reviewer; the producer fixes the failures and the reviewer spends effort only on what a script cannot decide.
clusters.merge_into: VE-R23 (its opening clause 'after scripts pass'); the general form is the frugality area's script-before-agent rule
clusters.evidence: REQ-306: 23 REVISEs in 30 verdicts over 14 hours; six of seven wave-2 REVISEs named no product defect; prejudge.sh found the same issues in 2 min 20 s. No after-figure recorded for #61 (pos.json:116), so the payoff is unmeasured.
clusters.why: Overturned: the measurement diagnoses judge waste, it does not show the checker paying, and pos.json:116 lists #61 as missing its after-figure. Not a separate rule; it is the ordering clause of VE-R23.

clusters.refined_rule: After the mechanical checks pass, one reviewer with fresh context who did not write the change re-runs them, reads each acceptance criterion against the evidence, and rejects only on a reproduced defect. Product defects go to the developer; test or harness defects to their author.
clusters.evidence: Against stacking: REQ-306 ran 14 hours, 81 agents, 23 REVISEs in 30 verdicts (pos.json waste). For one reviewer: REQ-029's rejection was proven by replaying the merge in an isolated clone (VE-168); REQ-066: only the judge's recount found 4 warnings. D160: a lane looped 3+ hours on harness items sent to the developer (VE-450). External: fresh-subagent review is recommended; multi-agent costs about 15x chat tokens (practices.json:22,33,47).
clusters.why: Stands, regraded measured -> incident: the measured figures show layered review wasting, the single reviewer's value rests on incidents and external guidance. Absorbs VE-R22.

clusters.refined_rule: On risky changes the implementer may not edit the proof tests and reports a wrong test instead; check by diffing the test paths.
clusters.evidence: No after-figure for directive #40; its local incidents (REQ-017b four rounds, REQ-023c three) predate the rule and REQ-136 is an incident against probe-first (an invalid probe was satisfied by loosening the generator). External support only: read-only tests beat instructions (practices.json:9,44).
clusters.why: Overturned: the cited incidents do not show the certifier-first relay paying. Only the tamper-resistance property has evidence (external), and it is the same test-path diff check as VE-R5.

clusters.refined_rule: Automated tests run only on named disposable accounts and devices reserved for testing. Never write to, log into or install over live production data or a device in use. Never type, guess or record a credential; report a blocked step as not run.
clusters.evidence: Pods force-stopped and wipe-installed the app under the owner mid-use, reported as 'the app crashed' (VE-392); a PIN copied from the owner's message was not the build's PIN and used 3 of 5 allowed attempts, locking a test device mid-session (VE-209, VE-356).
clusters.why: Stands: a human-owned, hard-to-reverse boundary with two incidents. One copy only; if the safety area holds it, this entry merges there.

clusters.refined_rule: Check the effect, not the command. A scripted preflight proves the environment is cleanly installed and confirms by checksum that the artifact under test is the one built. Deploy and release checks read config, signing and version from the artifact itself.
clusters.evidence: Reinstall-over kept old databases, hid a missing-column defect and produced 'fixed' results that were old data; an ASCII strings scan reported 0 for a UTF-16LE marker and deploy verification passed on the wrong build; a missing comma left ten indexes undeployable for over ten months (VE-536); a debug-key fallback shipped production artifacts debug-signed (VE-538).
clusters.why: Stands: four distinct incidents where the thing tested or shipped was not the thing built.

clusters.refined_rule: When agents share a machine or a stateful test environment, the runner takes a lock that caps heavy runs and gives the environment one user at a time; anyone blocked takes other work. Each parallel line of work verifies in its own tree with its own temp data.
clusters.evidence: Four agents running suites at once drove load average to 137 (peak 189) while the cap existed only as prose (VE-514); on 2026-10-07 every battery of a relaunch ran zero rows on a shared tree (VE-465); two test processes opened and deleted the same database file (VE-530). The suite lock's own effect is unmeasured (pos.json:76).
clusters.why: Stands as conditional (parallel work on one host). Enforcement changed hook -> script: the lock lives in the runner; a hook only needs to refuse a bare test command, which is implementation.

clusters.refined_rule: Verify cheapest first: static checks, unit tests, a quick smoke, then expensive device or owner-time checks. The expensive run refuses unless the cheap ones passed on the exact artifact.
clusters.evidence: A roughly 200k-token battery plus an owner login round ran against a build that wedged on launch (VE-540); REQ-110's fifteen debug lines cost two release builds and forty certifier turns (VE-433); a train gated green for ten minutes was then refused by the merge hook (VE-510).
clusters.why: Stands as a refusing script. The closing sentence ('scale to the diff; speed from automation, not skipping') was exhortation duplicating VE-R2 and was cut.

clusters.refined_rule: Pass a pinned clock into the code under test, derive fixture dates from the run's clock when production compares against real time, and force a race explicitly.
clusters.evidence: A test pinned now=2026-08-22 while the callee read the wall clock; its 7-day window elapsed and the suite went red with no code change. VE-486 is a predicted failure, not one that occurred.
clusters.why: Overturned: one real incident and one hypothetical, both test-writing traps, and VE-R12 already lists 'clock stepped back'. Two lines on VE-R12's page, not a standalone rule.

clusters.refined_rule: Before adding code, a helper or a test harness, name the nearest existing one and extend it; generate derived values from their source instead of copying.
clusters.merge_into: the no-duplicate-code rule (directive #54) in the outcome-driven or frugality area
clusters.evidence: One incident: four copies of one secret-scan grep failed every PR and fixing one copy broke the others (VE-535). Delta-only directives #23/#24 are unmeasured. External: agents regenerating existing code is a documented failure (practices.json:3,35,49).
clusters.why: Overturned: eighteen items, one incident, no measurement, and it is a development rule, not a verification rule. One copy belongs with #54; 'reviewers run the committed tests' is already in VE-R23.

clusters.refined_rule: Back a property stated in a comment, doc or verdict with an assertion or test that fails when it stops being true, or delete the statement. Never swallow an error silently. A timeout or limit that decides correctness cites a measurement a reader can open.
clusters.evidence: CO-008: a transport bound said to be supplied by an adapter timeout; grep for the timeout returned nothing (VE-284); placeholder nulls and zeros were read as fact by peers and swallowed sends counted as success (VE-562); REQ-030: a 60 s silence window could be shown false and an essential sync went heartbeat-silent (VE-251, VE-262).
clusters.why: Stands on three incidents; the silent-catch half already has a project gate (silent_noop_gate.sh).

clusters.refined_rule: Where code, design and plan disagree, ask whoever owns the decision instead of choosing. List every departure from the spec at the end of the fix note, including a value picked from an allowed range, with the check that would falsify it.
clusters.evidence: One incident: a '45-60 s' to 60 s choice, later falsified by the battery, had been buried in body prose (VE-256). The other three items are charter text with no recorded incident.
clusters.why: Kept narrowly: only the departures list is earned (one incident). 'Implement the agreed spec' was cut as something no rule needs to say. Weakest surviving rule in the area; drop it if the method needs trimming.

clusters.refined_rule: After removing code, list its callers and check each place it appeared; a step the removal made unreachable is a failure, not a skip.
clusters.merge_into: VE-R16 (enumerate callers and siblings); the real-run half is VE-R21 and VE-R18
clusters.evidence: REQ-053: removals shipped with unticked device boxes (VE-343): a skipped process step, with no defect recorded as escaping. The other items record nothing.
clusters.why: Overturned: the only 'incident' is non-compliance with a checkbox, not harm, so the evidence grade is none. The useful sentence is already VE-R16.

clusters.refined_rule: An end-to-end test saves its evidence as it goes: capture each step before the action that leaves it, write captures where a crash or timeout cannot lose them, and put a time bound on every watcher.
clusters.evidence: REQ-285: the runner hit its 900 s alarm and every screenshot was lost (VE-364); REQ-273: two of seven step screenshots showed the previous step (VE-365).
clusters.why: Stands on two incidents; lives in the shared test helper, so the method carries one line.

clusters.refined_rule: Where performance is gated, gate on deterministic counts. Use timing only from an alternating before/after comparison in one job, never a single run. Attribute an excess by reverting components one at a time before reworking any of them.
clusters.evidence: Single-run timing rounds spread 20-80% under load, so a 10% bar was superseded (VE-496, not re-opened by me). DECISIONS.md:9656-9668 (D1226, D1231): a x1.44 excess equal on both sizes tracked render-count ratios; per-widget revert arms were ordered and the app bar then targeted. Whether that removed the excess is not recorded there.
clusters.why: Kept, with the evidence corrected: the ruling claimed the revert arms 'found the app bar to be the cost'; D1231 only shows it targeted with another compare granted. Two source items from one REQ, so scope it to projects that gate performance.

clusters.refined_rule: Run bulk writes or deletes against a shared backend in stages: dry-run first, small throttled batches, a quiet window, and a saved copy of the original records.
clusters.evidence: Deleting 3,837 documents at once streamed removal events for minutes, held the shared sync debounce open and stalled menu, users and tables; the menu vanished from the POS.
clusters.why: Stands: a production outage from a hard-to-reverse act. One copy only; if the safety area holds it, this entry merges there.

clusters.refined_rule: Where older clients stay deployed, keep them working: no renames or shape changes to stored records, additive migrations with safe defaults, and a commit check that refuses a changed production identifier.
clusters.merge_into: VE-R38 (project rules file); the production-identifier freeze goes to the safety area as a human-owned act
clusters.evidence: none: docs/process/history/CLAUDE.md:831-838 states the constraint with no incident or measurement; scripts/gates/ddl_divergence_gate.sh exists as partial enforcement.
clusters.why: Overturned: no incident or figure in the evidence files or the history file. It is a fact about this product's deployment (old APKs in the field, a frozen Firebase project), which is what a project rules file is for, not a general method rule.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep incident-earned domain rules and deployment constraints in a project rules file that loads only with that code, each backed by a gate or test and its incident. They are not part of the general method.
clusters.evidence: Three shipped limit-window instances (orders 500, order_items 1000, local LIMIT 200) gave devices different sets; a status-filtered listener let a paid bill be tendered a second time; null overwrites erased a settled bill's captured charge; REQ-017b: three reworks fixed queue order one path at a time and a fourth path broke it (VE-186).
clusters.why: Stands; the POS list was removed from the rule wording so the transferable sentence is about where such rules live. Absorbs VE-R37.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep the project's checks inside its own repository so they run from a fresh clone.

clusters.refined_rule: Keep one short always-loaded rule list under a size budget checked by script. Admit an entry only with its incident or number and a date. At each review merge duplicates and delete what a script or broader rule covers. Procedures live in on-demand skills.

The prose lessons cap of about 30 did not hold (60 live lessons). Token effect after the cut was not measured.

clusters.refined_rule: Every guard has a logged, reasoned override, so a legitimate action always has a legal path. No speed or outcome-first mode switches a safety guard off. Keep each hook a thin wrapper over one policy script that the merge gate also runs.
